detail: SB 2807 took effect Sep 1, 2025; rules finalized Feb 2026, enforcement began May 28, 2026. Tesla holds a statewide TDLR transportation-network-company permit (valid to Aug 6, 2026), covering supervised and unsupervised operation.

Requires DMV permits for testing/deployment (with and without a safety driver) plus a separate CPUC permit to actually charge for rides. Tesla holds a testing permit and a CPUC charter-party carrier permit, but not yet a full driverless deployment permit as of mid-2026.

detail: Uses a lighter self-certification process for testing (granted Sep 2025) plus a statewide Transportation Network Company permit for paid rides (granted Nov 2025, approved in 4 days) — unlike California's city-by-city geofenced permits, Arizona's TNC authorization covers the entire state at once.

framework: Two very different outcomes — Tesla capped hard, Zoox cleared federally
detail: Tesla filed Jun 5, 2026 for an AVNC permit to run up to 5,000 vehicles across Clark County. The state granted it Jul 27 — but capped the fleet at just 10 vehicles, confined to the Strip, banned airport pickups, and set a 45 mph limit. Separately, on Jul 30, Zoox became the first company ever to win a federal NHTSA exemption for a robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals — cleared to charge fares on up to 2,500 vehicles/year, starting in Las Vegas.

sources.label: Zoox wins first federal no-controls exemption
